result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend bundling one subsetted family with a Roboto fallback, turn on tabular figures, and raise the question of which scripts the vendors read. B is slightly better: its stack includes system-ui before the generic family, its size and weight guidance is more concrete, and it gives a practical test on a real phone. A uses a little less font data and asks about scripts more directly, but it has small errors: Swahili does not need special diacritics, and the React Native syntax for tabular figures is off. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend one bundled face with tabular figures, offer a zero-byte Roboto-only option and flag script coverage. B is slightly stronger: it caps the payload more tightly (one variable file of about 100 KB, or two weights), names Noto Sans as the fallback for other scripts and ends by asking which languages are needed. A gives useful starting sizes but allows three static weights. It also says Roboto is on every Android phone, and B makes a smaller version of that assumption. B wrongly lists Swahili as needing diacritics.
